main_text.p: לָבַן Lateres formare, quasi Laterificare dicas: Futur. נִלְבְּנֶה Laterificemus, Formemus lateres, Genef.11.3. Et Infinit. לִלְבֹּן Ad formandum lateres, Exod.5.7.

מַלְבֵּן m. Fornax lateraria, Nah.3.14. וְהֶעֱבִיר אוֹתָם Et traduxit eos per fornacem lateriariam, id est, Combusit eos in loco ubi lateres urantur, 2.Samuel.12.31. & scriptum est cum Caph, sed juxta Masorethas legendum per Beth בְּמַלְבֵּן: Aut, ut Kimchi praeter praecedentem explicationem notat; Traduxit eos per Molecum, id est, Locum Moleci Dei Ammonitarum, in quo liberos traducebant per ignem, & comburebant eos. Sic idem sunt מלכן, מלכן, מלכם.

לָבַשׁ Vestivit se, Induit. Praeterit. וַיִּלְבַּשׁ בְּגָדִים Et induxit vestes alias, Levit.6.11. Et in Tzere, לָבַשׁ Psal.39.1. Chald. Futur. תִּלְבַּשׁ Indues vel Induëris, Dan.5.16. יִלְבַּשׁ Induetur, Dan.5.7. Pyh. Particip. מְלֻבָּשִׁים Induti, 1.Reg.22.10. Hiph. הִלְבִּישׁ Induere fecit, Induit, Vestivit alium: Praeter. וְהִלְבִּישָׁם Et indues eos, Exod.28.41. Chald. וְהַלְבִּישׁוּ לְדָנִיֵּאל Et induerunt Danielem, Dan.5.29.

לְבוּשׁ m. Indumentum, Vestimentum, Vestis; Esth.6. v.8. Aff. לְבוּשׁוֹ Indumentum suum, Genes.49.11. Plural. Constr. לִבְשֵׁי תְכֵלֶת Indutus hyacinthino, Ezech.23.6. Aff. בִּלְבָשֵׁיהֶם Vestimentis suis, Thren.4.14. Chald. לְבוּשֵׁהּ Vestimentum ejus, Dan.7.9. לְבוּשֵׁיהוֹן Vestimentis suis, Dan.3.21. Rabbini etiam foeminino utuntur לְבוּשָׁה, unde Talmudici: לְבוּשָׁה dicitur quasi לֹא בוּשָׁה Non pudor: Vestiendo enim & tegendo facit, ut hominem nuditatis suae non pudeat, Schabbath fol.77.2.
מַלְבּוּשׁ m. Idem, Job.27.16. Aff. וּמַלְבּוּשְׁךָ שֵׁשׁ Et vestimentum tuum fuit xylinum, sive byssinum, Ezech.16. v.13. Plu-

page.notes: Hebrew vowel points and some consonants are small and faint in the scan; the headwords, Chaldee forms and several Hebrew references are transcribed from best reading and may contain errors in vowel points, especially נִלְבְּנֶה, לִבְשֵׁי, לְבוּשֵׁיהוֹן and the Talmudic phrase לֹא בוּשָׁה. The Hebrew in "scriptum est" and "sunt מלכן, מלכן, מלכם" is printed without points and is copied as seen. The page ends mid-word with "Plu-" running on to the next page. A small mark "." before "explicationem" is a printer's separator and is not transcribed. Italic type is judged from the scan and may be incomplete.
